Eczema herpeticum requires immediate systemic antiviral therapy and often admission; look for monomorphic punched-out erosions and pain out of proportion [14,15]. Stop or hold immunosuppressive systemics. Involve ophthalmology for periocular disease. After recovery, redesign the AD plan to prevent the next severe flare—usually intensifying maintenance topicals or advancing disease-control therapy once safe. Document the episode prominently in the record. [14,15]

Hand, eyelid and genital AD need specialised vehicle and potency choices, plus contact-allergy thinking [6,11]. Night-time cotton gloves over emollient can help hand fissures. Eyelid disease favours TCI or mild TCS for very short courses. Occupational rehabilitation may be as important as pharmacology for hand disease. Avoid lidocaine/antibiotic cocktail creams that sensitise. [6,11,14]

Pregnancy pathways emphasise emollients, appropriate TCS, and early dermatology involvement before unplanned systemic exposure [11]. Discuss contraception before JAKi. Breastfeeding plans should consider product-specific data and topical nipple precautions. Uncontrolled severe AD itself threatens sleep, infection and mental health in pregnancy—treatment nihilism is not safer. Coordinate obstetric care in writing. [10,11]

Bangladesh escalation discipline: (1) emollient quantity confirmed, (2) site-correct TCS/TCI used, (3) infection/scabies/tinea excluded, (4) phototherapy considered if accessible, (5) systemic traditional or advanced agents only with monitoring capacity [7,8,10,11,20]. This sequence prevents mislabelling patients as biologic-refractory when basics were never delivered. Write the sequence in the notes for continuity across clinics. Advocate for formulary inclusion of essential emollients and TCS as public-health dermatology. [7,10,11,20]

For weeping facial flares, photograph before antibiotics when feasible, start antimicrobials promptly if bacterial infection is clear, and restore TCI/mild TCS as soon as crusting settles to prevent rebound lichenification [12,14,15]. Ask every new patient which pharmacy cream they last bought—names often reveal clobetasol combination misuse. Escalate systemic therapy only with a completed checklist uploaded or pasted into the chart [7,10,12].
Bacterial impetigo and cellulitis complicate excoriated AD; treat with targeted antimicrobials and maintain barrier repair [14,15].
Eczema herpeticum is a dermatologic emergency requiring systemic antivirals and immunosuppression hold [14,15].
Recurrent deep infections warrant immunodeficiency evaluation before further escalation [15].
Colonisation without clinical infection does not justify chronic systemic antibiotics [15].
Prolonged potent facial TCS causes atrophy, telangiectasia and dependency patterns—redirect to TCI and proactive plans [7,11].
TCI burning is usually early and transient; counsel to prevent abandonment [21].
JAKi and classical immunosuppressants demand laboratory and infection vigilance [8,29].
Unregulated combination creams are a major local harm pathway—ask and replace [7,11].
Chronic periocular AD and steroid exposure threaten eyes; prefer TCI and ophthalmology co-management [11,14].
Dupilumab ocular surface disease is manageable with early eye care [24].
Post-inflammatory dyspigmentation needs prevention via earlier control and avoidance of toxic bleaching [14].
Counsel that pigment lag does not equal treatment failure if itch and eczema are controlled [14].
Sleep loss, stigma and depression require explicit screening and often improve with disease control [14].
School/work letters and occupational adjustments are legitimate therapies [14].
Adolescent engagement prevents covert non-adherence [14].
Severe impairment despite clear skin should redirect to mental-health pathways [14].

prognosisQuantitative.estimate: EASI shows high inter- and intra-rater reliability for clinician-reported AD signs across body regions, supporting its use for baseline and follow-up severity tracking.
Validated banding of EASI (and related scores) into clear/mild/moderate/severe strata improves interpretability of absolute score changes in clinic and trials.
prognosisQuantitative.source: Chopra et al. British Journal of Dermatology

prognosisQuantitative.estimate: Cochrane synthesis supports moisturisers for improving eczema severity and reducing flares, with product choice guided by tolerability and adherence.
prognosisQuantitative.source: van Zuuren et al. Cochrane Review

prognosisQuantitative.estimate: Meta-analysis of randomised trials shows topical tacrolimus and pimecrolimus superior to vehicle for AD, informing steroid-sparing sensitive-site regimens.
Phase 3 trials demonstrated significantly higher rates of Investigator Static Global Assessment clear/almost clear with crisaborole 2% versus vehicle in mild-to-moderate AD.
In SOLO 1 and SOLO 2, dupilumab significantly increased the proportion of adults achieving IGA 0/1 with ≥2-point improvement versus placebo at 16 weeks.
Measure Up 1 and 2 showed once-daily upadacitinib achieved superior EASI-75 and validated IGA responses versus placebo in adolescents and adults with moderate-to-severe AD.
JADE MONO-1 demonstrated significant improvements in IGA and EASI-75 with abrocitinib versus placebo in adolescents and adults with moderate-to-severe AD.
Phase 3 monotherapy trials showed baricitinib improved validated severity endpoints versus placebo in patients with inadequate response to topical corticosteroids.
prognosisQuantitative.source: Simpson et al. British Journal of Dermatology

prognosisQuantitative.estimate: UK Working Party criteria retain useful positive predictive value for AD in population settings when the itchy-skin entry criterion plus discriminators are applied.
prognosisQuantitative.source: Williams et al. British Journal of Dermatology

prognosisQuantitative.estimate: EuroGuiDerm 2022 Part I provides graded recommendations positioning biologics and JAKi within systemic pathways for moderate-to-severe atopic eczema.

Contemporary Lancet reviews emphasise substantial adult burden and heterogeneous persistence trajectories, justifying long-term treat-to-control strategies rather than assumption of universal childhood resolution.

preciseDosing.indication: Facial/flexural AD and proactive steroid-sparing maintenance [11,21].
preciseDosing.standardDose: Apply a thin layer twice daily to active lesions until controlled, then consider twice-weekly proactive application to previous hotspots.
preciseDosing.doseReductionCriteria: Use 0.03% strength in younger children per label; reduce frequency if burning persists beyond early days after vehicle/technique advice.
preciseDosing.administration: Apply to clean dry skin on face/folds; avoid occlusive infected areas; continue daily emollients on surrounding skin; wash hands after non-facial application.
preciseDosing.onsetOffset: Stinging may occur at first applications; anti-inflammatory benefit typically builds over days to 2 weeks, with proactive use reducing subsequent flares.

preciseDosing.indication: Moderate-to-severe AD inadequately controlled by topicals [10,24].
preciseDosing.standardDose: 600 mg subcutaneous loading dose (usually two 300 mg injections), then 300 mg every 2 weeks.
preciseDosing.doseReductionCriteria: Paediatric patients use weight-based labelled dosing rather than adult empiric reduction; hold for serious hypersensitivity pending specialist review.
preciseDosing.renalAdjustment: No routine renal dose adjustment for standard AD dosing; assess overall infection risk in renal disease.
preciseDosing.hepaticAdjustment: No routine hepatic dose adjustment; review if severe hepatic impairment coexists with other risks.
preciseDosing.administration: Subcutaneous thigh/abdomen/upper arm rotation; train patient/caregiver; maintain cold chain; continue emollients and PRN topicals.
preciseDosing.onsetOffset: Itch often improves within 2–4 weeks; maximal cutaneous responses continue accruing through 16 weeks in pivotal trials.

preciseDosing.indication: Refractory moderate-to-severe AD with monitoring capacity [26,29].
preciseDosing.standardDose: 15 mg orally once daily, considering 30 mg daily for inadequate response in eligible adults per label and risk assessment.
preciseDosing.doseReductionCriteria: Prefer 15 mg with age, infection, cardiovascular or laboratory risk factors; avoid initiation in active serious infection or pregnancy.
preciseDosing.renalAdjustment: Follow label for severe renal impairment (dose restriction/avoidance as specified by jurisdiction).
preciseDosing.hepaticAdjustment: Follow label; often avoid in severe hepatic impairment.
preciseDosing.administration: Once daily with or without food per label; adhere to laboratory monitoring schedule; combine with topical foundation therapy.
preciseDosing.onsetOffset: Itch relief may begin within days; evaluate formal EASI/IGA response by 4–16 weeks while watching for infection and lab toxicity.

preciseDosing.indication: Short-course control of moderate body AD flares excluding face/folds [7,9].
preciseDosing.standardDose: Apply thinly once daily to active trunk/limb plaques using fingertip units for 5–14 days, then step down or convert to proactive twice-weekly use if appropriate.
preciseDosing.doseReductionCriteria: Shorten course on thinner skin or if early clearance occurs; never use as chronic daily facial therapy.
preciseDosing.administration: After emollient absorption or per local sequence preference; avoid occlusion unless specialist-directed; keep away from eyes and genitals.
preciseDosing.onsetOffset: Inflammation and itch often improve within several days; lichenification resolves more slowly over weeks with maintenance barrier care.
